title: A Cohen ring modulo p^n is formally smooth over Z/p^n
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $\Lambda$ a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] (a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ which is $p\Lambda$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]). Then for every $n\ge1$ the ring map $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is formally smooth (the case $\mathfrak n=0$ of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]). Explicitly, since a $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$-algebra is a ring in which $p^n=0$ and every ring homomorphism between such rings is $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$-linear: for every commutative ring $D$ with $p^nD=0$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/J$, and every ring homomorphism $g:\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\to D/J$, there is a ring homomorphism $f:\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0329 (lemma-cohen-ring-formally-smooth, line 44907) and its proof (Proposition Tag 0322 proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions for n = 1, Lemma Tag 031L lemma-lift-formal-smoothness, line 38100, for the induction); Cohen ring: Definition Tag 0327 (definition-cohen-ring)

proof.text: *The property $P(m)$.* For $m\ge1$ let $P(m)$ be the statement: for every commutative ring $D$ with $p^m\cdot1_D=0$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/J$, and every ring homomorphism $g:\Lambda/p^m\Lambda\to D/J$, there is a ring homomorphism $f:\Lambda/p^m\Lambda\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. $P(m)$ says exactly that $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^m\Lambda$ is formally smooth in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] with $\mathfrak n=0$: there $g(\mathfrak n^k)=g(0)=0$ holds for $k=1$, so the condition is lifting of all algebra maps; a ring map $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z\to D$ exists iff $p^m\cdot1_D=0$ and is then unique ($1\mapsto1$), it makes $D/J$ a $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z$-algebra through $q$, and a ring homomorphism between $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z$-algebras is $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z$-linear, since $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z$ consists of the classes of integers $N$ and $h(N\cdot x)=N\cdot h(x)$ for any additive $h$. The item's statement is $P(n)$ for all $n\ge1$.

proof.text: *Base case $n=1$.* $\Lambda/p\Lambda=\kappa$ is a field of characteristic $p$ (step 2(a)). Let $D$ be a commutative ring with $p\cdot1_D=0$, $J\subseteq D$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, $q:D\to D/J$ the quotient map and $g:\kappa\to D/J$ a ring homomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-nilpotent-lifting] with $K=\kappa$ and $N=2$ there is a ring homomorphism $f:\kappa\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. This is $P(1)$. (Stacks deduces this from Proposition 0322 applied to $\kappa/\mathbf F_p$, which is separable since $\mathbf F_p$ is perfect; that argument is the source of the cited node.)

proof.text: *Flatness of $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^m\Lambda$.* Let $m\ge1$. $\mathbf Z$ is a principal ideal domain and $\Lambda$ is a torsion-free $\mathbf Z$-module (step 2(b)), so $\Lambda$ is a flat $\mathbf Z$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat] with $R=\mathbf Z$, the ideal $p^m\mathbf Z$ and $M=\Lambda$, the module $\Lambda/p^m\Lambda$ is a flat $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z$-module for $(r\bmod p^m)\cdot(x\bmod p^m\Lambda)=rx\bmod p^m\Lambda$. Since $rx=(r\cdot1_\Lambda)x$, this is the module structure given by the ring map $\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^m\Lambda$, $r\bmod p^m\mapsto r\cdot1\bmod p^m\Lambda$; so this ring map is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: *Induction step.* Let $n\ge1$ and assume $P(n)$. Put $R=\mathbf Z/p^{n+1}\mathbf Z$, $S=\Lambda/p^{n+1}\Lambda$ with the canonical ring map $\varphi:R\to S$, and $I=p^nR$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-formal-smoothness-flat-square-zero]: (1) $I^2=p^{2n}R=0$ as $2n\ge n+1$; (2) $\varphi$ is flat by step 4 with $m=n+1$; (3) $R/I=\mathbf Z/(p^{n+1},p^n)=\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$ and $IS=p^n S$, so $S/IS=\Lambda/(p^{n+1}\Lambda+p^n\Lambda)=\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$, and the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is the canonical map $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$, which is formally smooth by $P(n)$ and step 1. Hence $\varphi:\mathbf Z/p^{n+1}\mathbf Z\to\Lambda/p^{n+1}\Lambda$ is formally smooth (lifting along square-zero ideals for $R$-algebras), which is $P(n+1)$ by step 1.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0329 (lemma-cohen-ring-formally-smooth, line 44907), proof, induction: Lemma Tag 031L (lemma-lift-formal-smoothness, line 38100) for Z/p^{n+1} -> Lambda/p^{n+1}Lambda and I = (p^n)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 3, $P(1)$ holds, and by step 5, $P(n)$ implies $P(n+1)$ for every $n\ge1$; by induction $P(n)$ holds for every $n\ge1$, which by step 1 is the statement.
